title: Restricted coefficient push mate is the regular-coefficient projection map
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, with $p\ne\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism. Let $a:R\to S$ be a morphism of commutative condensed rings such that extension of scalars is exact on every scheme [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]. Write $R_Z=p_Z^*R$, $S_Z=p_Z^*S$ for $Z=X,Y$, with the canonical compatible coefficient inverse-image isomorphisms [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]. Work in the ordinary unbounded internal-module derived categories, identified with sheaf-module derived categories by [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison]. Put $T_Z=S_Z\otimes^L_{R_Z}-$ and let $U_Z$ be exact scalar restriction; put $L_R=Lf_R^*$, $L_S=Lf_S^*$, $G_R=Rf_{R*}$, $G_S=Rf_{S*}$, with their specified scalar and geometric adjunctions [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. Set $C=U_YS_Y$, $B=U_XS_X$, considered in degree zero, and let $\rho:L_RC\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ be the canonical restricted-regular pullback identification. Let $e_Z(M):U_ZT_ZM\xrightarrow{\sim}M\otimes^L_{R_Z}U_ZS_Z$ be the canonical balanced scalar-tensor identification, using symmetry to put the coefficient on the right [lem-sfb-internal-scalar-pullback-normalization].
Let $\gamma:T_YG_R\to G_ST_X$ be the coefficient mate [def-sfb-derived-push-hom], and let $d:U_YG_S\xrightarrow{\sim}G_RU_X$ be [def-sfb-derived-comap-lower-star-iso]. For every $K\in D(R_X)$ define the specified restricted map
$$h_K=G_R(e_X(K))\circ d_{T_XK}\circ U_Y(\gamma_K)\circ e_Y(G_RK)^{-1}:
G_RK\otimes^L C\longrightarrow G_R(K\otimes^L B).$$
Then its $L_R\dashv G_R$ transpose is exactly
$$(\varepsilon^R_K\otimes1_B)\circ(1\otimes\rho)\circ\mu_{G_RK,C}.$$
Consequently $h_K=G_R(1_K\otimes\rho)\circ\delta_{K,C}$, where $\delta_{K,C}:G_RK\otimes^L C\to G_R(K\otimes^L L_RC)$ is the canonical projection map, defined as the adjunct of $(\varepsilon^R_K\otimes1)\circ\mu_{G_RK,C}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. This equality is natural in $K$. No boundedness, qcqs, constructibility, filtered diagram, stage projection isomorphism or invertibility of $h_K$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_symm to the specified geometric and scalar adjunctions and the inverse of the actual derivedComapLowerStarIso. Applying the geometric mate equivalence identifies actual derivedPushHom with rho of flatScalarTheta; this is scalarMate_eq.

Use flat_coefficient_square_normalization for its actual direct-image identification and PullNormalized clause. Apply internal_scalar_mate_projection to that normalized theta and the supplied normalized tensor presentations. Cancel the tensor-presentation isomorphism to obtain restrictedMap = scalarProjection, together with naturality.

Identify the two regular-coefficient pullback isomorphisms. Cancel scalarRestrictionPull and pullback of scalarCoefficientUnit, use naturality of the exact-localization comparison, and the exact-functor composition and natural-isomorphism compatibilities with degree zero. The ordinary comapUpperStarIso cancels its inverse. The derived unit is the exact-functor single comparison followed by the ordinary unit map, by the defining left-derived counit and localization naturality.

The mate-induced ordinary pullback monoidal structure equals the canonical one by uniqueness of the normalized pushforward pairing and injectivity of Monoidal.toOplaxMonoidal. Apply leftDerivedUpperStarTensor_eq_leftDerivedTensorComparison. Thus internalProjection and moduleObjectProjectionMap have identical counit transposes, and scalarProjection is the displayed projection followed by direct image of identity tensor regularPullback.

Transpose the equality using naturality of the adjunction hom equivalence. Cancel homEquiv with its inverse and use naturality of the tensor bifunctor in the regular-coefficient pullback. This gives the first clause; the previous equality gives the second, and the naturality clause of internal_scalar_mate_projection gives the third.
